name: Rice Bowls
summary: Brown rice in modest portions, always with beans or vegetables piled on top: a cooked-salmon poke-style bowl, a turkey burrito bowl, a chicken stir-fry, a red lentil dal and a beef bibimbap-style bowl. Fish four times, never raw, and four dishes that cook once and make tomorrow's lunch.
howItWorks:
**Rice, in modest portions.** Every bowl starts on brown rice or brown basmati and is piled high with beans, lentils, edamame or vegetables like kale and broccoli. Rice, brown rice especially, takes up more arsenic than other grains, so dinners rinse it and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, then drain it, which lowers it. The oat breakfasts give the rice a rest.

**Cook once, eat twice.** Tuesday's burrito bowl, Wednesday's stir-fry, Thursday's dal and Saturday's bibimbap each make two portions, so the next lunch is done, and three lunches use ready-cooked rice from a pouch. Cool cooked rice within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep it up to 3 days and reheat it once until steaming hot. Avocado, salsa, yogurt and the firm fried egg go on fresh.

**Fish, always cooked.** Monday's salmon poke-style bowl, Friday's turmeric-lemon trout, Saturday's sardine bowl and Sunday's yogurt-spiced salmon, plus a sardine snack on Thursday, bring omega-3 and some **vitamin D**, which is hard to get from food. Fish is never a leftover. Beef, turkey, chicken, lentils and eggs cover the rest of the protein.

**What changes with size.** Light keeps most of the rice and trims the fish, meat, oil, nuts and some beans, drops a snack a day, and adds spinach to two bowls and a firm egg to the dal. Near 1,800 kcal, Standard halves the rice first. Big adds a snack a day, two on Saturday, and grows the rice, meat, fish, beans and nuts as calories rise.

recipes.name: Savoury ginger-soy oats with mushrooms, spinach and edamame
recipes.about: Creamy oats cooked in water with ginger and soy, topped with golden mushrooms, wilted spinach and warm edamame and a drizzle of sesame oil, with a glass of milk on the side. The edamame and oats bring **protein and fibre**, and the spinach brings iron and folate.
steps: Wash the mushrooms and spinach and slice the mushrooms. Pour hot water over the frozen edamame until steaming hot all the way through, then drain.
Bring the oats, grated ginger and 250 ml of water to a gentle simmer in a small pot, stirring, until thick and creamy, about 6 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a nonstick pan and cook the mushrooms until golden, about 4 minutes. Add the spinach and soy sauce and stir until the spinach wilts.
Spoon the oats into a bowl, top with the mushrooms, spinach and edamame, drizzle with the sesame oil and serve with a glass of milk.
recipes.tip: Add a splash of water if the oats thicken as they stand.
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese savoury rice porridge, made with oats

recipes.name: Warm cinnamon pear over Greek yogurt with oat and almond crunch
recipes.about: Cold Greek yogurt under soft pear simmered with cinnamon and a little ginger, topped with a crunchy toasted oat and almond mix. The yogurt brings **protein and calcium**, and the pear and oats bring fibre.
steps: Toast the oats and almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes. Tip them out to cool.
Wash the pear and dice it. Simmer it in the same pan with the cinnamon, ginger and a splash of water until soft, about 5 minutes.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the warm pear and scatter over the crunch.
recipes.tip: Toast a few days' worth of crunch at once and keep it in a jar.

recipes.name: Savoury brown rice breakfast bowl with kale, mushrooms and firm egg
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean and Chinese savoury rice breakfasts
recipes.about: Warm brown rice stir-fried with mushrooms and kale, topped with firm scrambled egg and a drizzle of sesame oil, with a glass of milk on the side. **Eggs and mushrooms** bring choline and B vitamins, and the kale brings calcium and vitamin K.

ingredients.note: ready-cooked pouch or frozen, or rice cooked and chilled earlier

steps: Wash the kale and mushrooms, slice the mushrooms and thinly slice the kale. Beat the eggs with a splash of water.
Warm the olive oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms until golden, about 4 minutes, then add the kale and a splash of water and stir until it is tender, about 3 minutes.
Add the rice and soy sauce and stir until it is steaming hot all the way through. Push everything to one side.
Pour the eggs into the empty side and stir until completely set and firm, about 2 minutes, then mix them through.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with the sesame oil and serve with a glass of milk.
recipes.tip: Microwave a pouch of rice for 2 minutes. Rice from a previous night must have been cooled within 1 hour in a shallow container and used within 3 days; reheat it until steaming hot.

recipes.name: Cumin chicken, lentil and roasted vegetable brown rice bowl with lemon yogurt
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern roasted chicken and lentil rice bowls
recipes.about: Chicken breast, carrot, zucchini and cherry tomatoes roasted with cumin and paprika, piled on brown rice with warm lentils, wilted spinach, a cool lemon-yogurt sauce and parsley. The lentils and spinach bring **iron, folate and fibre**, and the lemon helps your body absorb that iron.

ingredients.note: ready-cooked pouch or frozen, or rice cooked and chilled earlier

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the carrot, zucchini, tomatoes, spinach and parsley. Slice the carrot thinly so it cooks quickly.

Toss the chicken, carrot, zucchini, onion and tomatoes on a tray with the oil, cumin, paprika and most of the salt. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken. Roast until the carrot is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir the yogurt, half of the lemon juice, the rest of the salt and a spoonful of water together. Heat the rice and the lentils separately, until steaming hot.
Stir the spinach into the hot tray for a minute, until it wilts.
Spoon the rice into a bowl, top with the lentils and the roasted chicken and vegetables, and drizzle with the yogurt sauce. Squeeze over the rest of the lemon and finish with the parsley.
recipes.tip: Packing it? Cook it the night before, cool the chicken, vegetables, rice and lentils in a shallow container in the fridge within 1 hour and keep the yogurt sauce apart. Carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack, reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), add the sauce and eat it the same day.

recipes.name: Warm ginger-soy chickpeas with kale, red pepper and egg over brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-style soy-ginger stir-fried greens and beans
recipes.about: Chickpeas, red pepper and wilted kale stir-fried with ginger, soy sauce and a drizzle of sesame oil, spooned over brown rice with a firm hard-boiled egg, lemon, cilantro and toasted walnuts. The chickpeas and kale bring **iron, folate and calcium**, and the lemon and pepper bring vitamin C to help absorb the iron.

ingredients.note: boiled until the yolk is firm, as in the steps
ready-cooked pouch or frozen, or rice cooked and chilled earlier

steps: Lower the egg into boiling water and boil it for 10 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm, then cool it under cold water and peel it. Wash the kale, pepper and cilantro, slice the pepper and onion, grate the ginger and chop the kale, discarding the thick stems.
Warm the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft and starting to brown, about 8 minutes. Stir in the ginger and soy sauce for 30 seconds.
Add the kale and a splash of water, cover and cook until the kale is tender, about 4 minutes. Stir in the chickpeas and salt and heat until steaming hot. Heat the rice until steaming.
Season with the lemon juice. Spoon over the rice, halve the egg and set it on top, and finish with the cilantro, walnuts and a drizzle of sesame oil.
recipes.tip: Packing it? Make it the night before and cool it in a shallow container in the fridge within 1 hour. Carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack, reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and eat it the same day.

recipes.name: Lemony sardine, edamame and cucumber brown rice bowl
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Portuguese and Greek sardine and rice salads
recipes.about: Canned sardines flaked over brown rice with edamame, cucumber and parsley, finished with a lemon-yogurt dressing and a few almonds. The sardines bring **omega-3, calcium and vitamin D**, and the edamame adds fibre and protein.

ingredients.note: ready-cooked pouch or frozen, or rice cooked and chilled earlier

steps: Pour boiling water over the frozen edamame, or microwave them, until steaming hot all the way through, then drain. Heat the rice until steaming and let it cool a few minutes.
Wash the cucumber and parsley. Slice the cucumber and chop the parsley.
Stir the yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper together.
Pile the rice, edamame and cucumber in a bowl, flake the sardines on top and spoon over the dressing. Finish with the parsley and almonds.
recipes.tip: Keep an opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. Packing it? Spread the heated rice in a shallow container and chill it within 1 hour before you build the bowl, then carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

recipes.name: Cooked salmon poke-style bowl with spicy yogurt drizzle
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Hawaiian poke bowls, with the salmon fully cooked
recipes.about: Cubes of soy-ginger salmon, cooked through and served warm over brown rice with cool edamame, cucumber and carrot ribbons. A spicy lemon-yogurt drizzle ties it together. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the edamame brings protein and folate.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.
Meanwhile, pour hot water over the frozen edamame until steaming hot all the way through, then drain. Wash the cucumber and carrot, slice the cucumber and peel the carrot into ribbons.
Stir the yogurt, chili, half of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt together for the drizzle. Stir the soy sauce, ginger and sesame oil together for the glaze.

Warm a nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Add the salmon cubes and cook, turning, until opaque and flaky and at least 70 °C (158 °F) inside, 4 to 5 minutes. Pour in the glaze for the last minute so it coats the fish. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Spoon the rice into a bowl and arrange the salmon, edamame, cucumber and carrot on top. Squeeze over the rest of the lemon and drizzle with the spicy yogurt.
recipes.tip: Not a fan of heat? Leave out the chili. The salmon is never served raw here. Put the rice on first.

recipes.name: Smoky turkey and black bean burrito bowl
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex burrito bowls
recipes.about: Smoky, cumin-spiced ground turkey and black beans with sweet pepper over brown rice, finished with fresh tomato salsa, creamy avocado and cilantro. The beans and turkey bring **protein, iron and fibre**, and the tomato and pepper bring vitamin C.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the turkey and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands, board and spoon after handling the raw turkey.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika and salt for 1 minute. Add the beans and a splash of water and simmer until hot and the sauce clings, about 4 minutes.
Mix the tomatoes with half of the lemon juice and the cilantro for a quick salsa. Wash the avocado before cutting it.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the turkey and beans, then the salsa and avocado, and squeeze over the rest of the lemon.

Before adding the cold toppings, pack the second portion of rice, turkey and beans into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), then add fresh toppings.
recipes.tip: The rice, beans and turkey freeze well without the toppings: cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze. Put the rice on first.

recipes.name: Ginger chicken, broccoli and edamame stir-fry with walnuts
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-American chicken and broccoli
recipes.about: Tender chicken breast with broccoli, edamame, carrot and mushrooms in a glossy ginger-garlic sauce, over brown rice with a handful of wilted spinach and toasted walnuts. **Broccoli, edamame and spinach** bring vitamin C, folate and iron, and the chicken brings protein.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.
Meanwhile, stir the soy sauce, ginger, garlic and 3 tablespoons of water together in a small bowl. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, about 3 minutes, and set aside.

Heat half of the oil in a large pan or wok over high heat. Cook the chicken in a single layer, turning, until golden and at least 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, about 6 minutes. Move it to a plate and wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.

Add the rest of the oil and the broccoli, carrot, mushrooms and frozen edamame with a splash of water. Stir-fry until the broccoli is bright green and just tender and the edamame is steaming hot all the way through, about 6 minutes.
Return the chicken and add the spinach, pour in the sauce and stir until the spinach wilts and the sauce is glossy and bubbling, about 1 minute. Finish with the sesame oil.

Spoon over the rice and top with the walnuts. Pack the second portion, without the walnuts, into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Add a splash of water when reheating so the sauce loosens. Put the rice on first.

recipes.name: Red lentil and kale dal with brown basmati
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian masoor dal
recipes.about: A soft, golden dal of red lentils, tomato and kale with ginger, garlic, cumin and garam masala, served over brown basmati with a cool cucumber side and a spoonful of yogurt. The lentils and kale bring **iron, folate and calcium**, and the lemon helps your body absorb that iron.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain and fluff it.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds until they sizzle, about 30 seconds, then add the onion and cook until soft and golden, about 7 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric and chili for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, lentils, salt and 3 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, stirring now and then, until the lentils have collapsed into a thick soup, about 15 minutes. Add water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the kale and garam masala and simmer until the kale is tender, about 6 minutes, then finish with the lemon juice. Toss the cucumber with the cilantro.

Serve the dal over the rice with the cucumber and a spoonful of yogurt on the side. Cool the second portion of dal and rice within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep the yogurt and cucumber separate, and refrigerate. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), with a splash of water.
recipes.tip: To freeze the dal, cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge and use within 2 days, never refreezing. Reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Put the rice on first.

recipes.name: Turmeric-lemon trout with green herb rice and roast broccoli
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Persian sabzi polo ba mahi, herbed rice with fish
recipes.about: A trout fillet rubbed with turmeric and garlic and roasted next to broccoli, served on brown basmati tossed with kale, parsley, cilantro and dill, with plenty of lemon. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the kale and broccoli bring vitamin C, vitamin K and folate.

ingredients.note: skin on or off, pin bones removed

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the kale, broccoli, parsley and cilantro. Finely chop the kale and the herbs and cut the broccoli into florets.

Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, 25 to 30 minutes, adding the kale for the last 2 minutes. Drain well. Meanwhile, toss the broccoli with a little of the oil and a pinch of the salt on a lined tray and roast for 10 minutes.
Rub the trout with the turmeric, half of the garlic, a little oil, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Push the broccoli to one side, lay the trout on the tray and roast until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F), 10 to 12 minutes.
Warm the rest of the oil and garlic in the empty rice pot for 30 seconds, then tip the rice and kale back in with the dill, parsley, cilantro and half of the lemon juice and stir.
Serve the trout on the herb rice with the broccoli, and squeeze over the rest of the lemon.
recipes.tip: Put the rice on first. No dried dill? Use a little more parsley.

recipes.name: Beef bibimbap-style bowl with sesame vegetables and chili-lemon sauce
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean bibimbap, with a soy-garlic beef and a chili-lemon sauce in place of gochujang
recipes.about: Thin soy-garlic beef over brown rice with separate little piles of sesame spinach, carrot, zucchini, mushrooms and edamame, finished with a chili-lemon sauce you stir through at the table. The vegetables bring **vitamin A, folate and fibre** (the edamame adds protein), and the beef brings iron and zinc.

ingredients.note: sliced very thinly across the grain

steps: Mix half of the soy sauce, the garlic, half of the sesame oil and a few grinds of pepper with the beef. Marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes, never reusing the marinade for anything else. Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.
Meanwhile, stir the gochugaru, lemon juice, the rest of the soy sauce and a spoonful of water together for the sauce.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, drain it and squeeze it dry. Toss it with a little of the sesame oil and the salt.
Pour hot water over the frozen edamame until steaming hot all the way through, then drain, and keep it as its own pile.

Warm a little of the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the carrot, zucchini and mushrooms separately, each for 2 to 4 minutes until just tender, with a pinch of salt, keeping the piles apart.

Cook the beef in the rest of the oil over high heat, in two batches, until browned and at least 71 °C (160 °F), about 3 minutes a batch. Wash your hands, board, knife and tongs after handling the raw beef.
Fry the eggs in the nonstick pan with the last of the olive oil, flip them and cook until the whites and yolks are completely firm, about 4 minutes in all.
Put the rice in bowls and arrange the beef, edamame and vegetables on top in separate piles. Top each with a firm egg, finish with the remaining sesame oil and serve with the sauce to stir through.

Pack the second portion without the egg, with the sauce on the side, into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), then add the sauce. Fry a fresh firm egg to go on top.
recipes.tip: Short on time? Skip the zucchini and use extra spinach. Use less gochugaru for less heat. Put the rice on first.

recipes.name: Yogurt-spiced salmon with kale and chickpea masala over brown basmati
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian tandoori-style fish and chana masala
recipes.about: Salmon fillet marinated in lemony yogurt and warm spices and roasted until flaky, served over brown basmati with a quick tomato, kale and chickpea masala. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the chickpeas and kale bring fibre, iron and calcium.
steps: Mix the yogurt, half of the lemon juice, half of the garam masala, the turmeric, half of the salt and half of the garlic and ginger. Coat the salmon and marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes, never reusing the marinade. Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.

Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a tray. Lift the salmon onto the tray, leaving the extra marinade behind, and roast until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F), 10 to 12 minutes. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds until they sizzle, then the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the rest of the garlic and ginger, the rest of the garam masala and the chili for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, the rest of the salt and a splash of water and simmer until the tomatoes collapse, about 6 minutes. Stir in the kale and simmer until tender, about 5 minutes, then finish with the rest of the lemon juice.
Serve the salmon over the rice with the chickpea masala spooned alongside and the cilantro scattered over.
recipes.tip: Leave out the chili for a mild version. Put the rice on first.

recipes.name: Apple with almonds
recipes.about: A crisp apple with a small handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the almonds.

recipes.name: Pear with walnuts
recipes.about: A juicy pear with a few walnuts. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**, and the pear brings fibre.
steps: Wash the pear, slice it and serve with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Orange with walnuts
recipes.about: A juicy orange with a few walnuts. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**, and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the orange, peel and segment it, and serve with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Apple slices with walnuts and cinnamon
recipes.about: Crisp apple slices with a few walnuts and a shake of cinnamon. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it, dust with the cinnamon and serve with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
recipes.about: A banana with a few walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**, and the banana brings potassium.
steps: Slice the banana, dust with the cinnamon and serve with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Warm edamame with lemon and chili
recipes.about: Warm edamame with lemon, a pinch of chili and a little salt. The edamame brings **protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Pour boiling water over the frozen edamame, or microwave them, until steaming hot all the way through, then drain.
Toss with the lemon, chili and salt.

recipes.name: Carrot and cucumber sticks with lemony yogurt dip
recipes.about: Crunchy carrot and cucumber sticks with a cool lemon-yogurt dip. The yogurt brings **calcium and protein**, and the carrot brings vitamin A.
steps: Wash the carrot and cucumber and cut them into sticks.
Stir the yogurt, lemon juice, salt and pepper together and serve with the sticks.

recipes.name: Lemony sardines with cucumber and cherry tomatoes
recipes.about: A small plate of canned sardines with cucumber, cherry tomatoes, lemon and parsley. The sardines bring **omega-3, calcium and vitamin B12**, and the lemon and tomatoes brighten them.
steps: Wash the cucumber, tomatoes and parsley, then slice the cucumber, halve the tomatoes and chop the parsley.
Arrange the vegetables on a plate, lay the sardines alongside, and finish with the lemon juice, parsley and pepper.
recipes.tip: Keep an opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Blueberries with walnuts
recipes.about: A bowl of blueberries with a few walnuts. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**, and the blueberries bring vitamin C and fibre.
steps: Rinse the blueberries and serve with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Pear with almonds
recipes.about: A juicy pear with a small handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the pear brings fibre.
steps: Wash the pear, slice it and serve with the almonds.

recipes.name: Orange with almonds
recipes.about: A juicy orange with a small handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E, magnesium and a little calcium**, and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the orange, peel and segment it, and serve with the almonds.

recipes.name: Banana with almonds and cinnamon
recipes.about: A banana with a few almonds and a dusting of cinnamon. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the banana brings potassium.

Meanwhile, stir the yogurt, half of the lemon juice, the rest of the salt and a spoonful of water together. Heat the rice and the lentils separately, until steaming hot.
Stir the spinach into the hot tray for a minute, until it wilts.
Spoon the rice into a bowl, top with the lentils and the roasted chicken and vegetables, and drizzle with the yogurt sauce. Squeeze over the rest of the lemon and finish with the parsley.
recipes.tip: Packing it? Cook it the night before, cool the chicken, vegetables, rice and lentils in a shallow container in the fridge within 1 hour and keep the yogurt sauce apart. Carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack, reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), add the sauce and eat it the same day.

recipes.name: Warm ginger-soy chickpeas with kale, red pepper and egg over brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-style soy-ginger stir-fried greens and beans
recipes.about: Chickpeas, red pepper and wilted kale stir-fried with ginger, soy sauce and a drizzle of sesame oil, spooned over brown rice with a firm hard-boiled egg, lemon, cilantro and toasted walnuts. The chickpeas and kale bring **iron, folate and calcium**, and the lemon and pepper bring vitamin C to help absorb the iron.

ingredients.note: boiled until the yolk is firm, as in the steps
ready-cooked pouch or frozen, or rice cooked and chilled earlier

steps: Lower the egg into boiling water and boil it for 10 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm, then cool it under cold water and peel it. Wash the kale, pepper and cilantro, slice the pepper and onion, grate the ginger and chop the kale, discarding the thick stems.
Warm the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft and starting to brown, about 8 minutes. Stir in the ginger and soy sauce for 30 seconds.
Add the kale and a splash of water, cover and cook until the kale is tender, about 4 minutes. Stir in the chickpeas and salt and heat until steaming hot. Heat the rice until steaming.
Season with the lemon juice. Spoon over the rice, halve the egg and set it on top, and finish with the cilantro, walnuts and a drizzle of sesame oil.
recipes.tip: Packing it? Make it the night before and cool it in a shallow container in the fridge within 1 hour. Carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack, reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and eat it the same day.

recipes.name: Smoky turkey and black bean burrito bowl
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex burrito bowls
recipes.about: Smoky, cumin-spiced ground turkey and black beans with sweet pepper over brown rice, finished with fresh tomato salsa, creamy avocado and cilantro. The beans and turkey bring **protein, iron and fibre**, and the tomato and pepper bring vitamin C.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the turkey and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands, board and spoon after handling the raw turkey.

Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika and salt for 1 minute. Add the beans and a splash of water and simmer until hot and the sauce clings, about 4 minutes. Stir in the spinach for the last minute, until it wilts.
Mix the tomatoes with half of the lemon juice and the cilantro for a quick salsa. Wash the avocado before cutting it.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the turkey and beans, then the salsa and avocado, and squeeze over the rest of the lemon.

Before adding the cold toppings, pack the second portion of rice, turkey and beans into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), then add fresh toppings.
recipes.tip: The rice, beans and turkey freeze well without the toppings: cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze. Put the rice on first.

recipes.name: Ginger chicken, broccoli and edamame stir-fry with walnuts
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-American chicken and broccoli
recipes.about: Tender chicken breast with broccoli, edamame, carrot and mushrooms in a glossy ginger-garlic sauce, over brown rice with a handful of wilted spinach and toasted walnuts. **Broccoli, edamame and spinach** bring vitamin C, folate and iron, and the chicken brings protein.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.
Meanwhile, stir the soy sauce, ginger, garlic and 3 tablespoons of water together in a small bowl. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, about 3 minutes, and set aside.

Heat half of the oil in a large pan or wok over high heat. Cook the chicken in a single layer, turning, until golden and at least 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, about 6 minutes. Move it to a plate and wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.

Add the rest of the oil and the broccoli, carrot, mushrooms and frozen edamame with a splash of water. Stir-fry until the broccoli is bright green and just tender and the edamame is steaming hot all the way through, about 6 minutes.
Return the chicken and add the spinach, pour in the sauce and stir until the spinach wilts and the sauce is glossy and bubbling, about 1 minute. Finish with the sesame oil.

Spoon over the rice and top with the walnuts. Pack the second portion, without the walnuts, into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Add a splash of water when reheating so the sauce loosens. Put the rice on first.

recipes.name: Red lentil and kale dal with brown basmati and a firm egg
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian masoor dal
recipes.about: A soft, golden dal of red lentils, tomato and kale with ginger, garlic, cumin and garam masala, served over brown basmati with a firm boiled egg, a cool cucumber side and a spoonful of yogurt. The lentils and kale bring **iron, folate and calcium**, the egg adds choline, and the lemon helps your body absorb the iron.

ingredients.note: boiled until the yolk is firm, as in the steps

steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain and fluff it.
Put the eggs, one for each portion, in a small pot of cold water, bring to a boil and boil 10 minutes, until the yolks are completely firm. Cool them under cold water.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds until they sizzle, about 30 seconds, then add the onion and cook until soft and golden, about 7 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric and chili for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, lentils, salt and 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, stirring now and then, until the lentils have collapsed into a thick soup, about 15 minutes. Add water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the kale and garam masala and simmer until the kale is tender, about 6 minutes, then finish with the lemon juice. Toss the cucumber with the cilantro.

Serve the dal over the rice with one egg, peeled and halved, the cucumber and a spoonful of yogurt on the side. Cool the second portion of dal and rice within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep the yogurt and cucumber separate, and refrigerate it with the second egg still in its shell. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), with a splash of water.
recipes.tip: To freeze the dal, without the egg, cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge and use within 2 days, never refreezing. Reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Put the rice on first.

recipes.name: Lemony sardine, edamame and cucumber brown rice bowl
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Portuguese and Greek sardine and rice salads
recipes.about: Canned sardines flaked over brown rice with edamame, cucumber and parsley, finished with a lemon-yogurt dressing and a few almonds. The sardines bring **omega-3, calcium and vitamin D**, and the edamame adds fibre and protein.

ingredients.note: ready-cooked pouch or frozen, or rice cooked and chilled earlier

steps: Pour boiling water over the frozen edamame, or microwave them, until steaming hot all the way through, then drain. Heat the rice until steaming and let it cool a few minutes.
Wash the cucumber and parsley. Slice the cucumber and chop the parsley.
Stir the yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper together.
Pile the rice, edamame and cucumber in a bowl, flake the sardines on top and spoon over the dressing. Finish with the parsley and almonds.
recipes.tip: Keep an opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. Packing it? Spread the heated rice in a shallow container and chill it within 1 hour before you build the bowl, then carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

recipes.name: Beef bibimbap-style bowl with sesame vegetables and chili-lemon sauce
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean bibimbap, with a soy-garlic beef and a chili-lemon sauce in place of gochujang
recipes.about: Thin soy-garlic beef over brown rice with separate little piles of sesame spinach, carrot, zucchini, mushrooms and edamame, finished with a chili-lemon sauce you stir through at the table. The vegetables bring **vitamin A, folate and fibre** (the edamame adds protein), and the beef brings iron and zinc.

ingredients.note: sliced very thinly across the grain

steps: Mix half of the soy sauce, the garlic, half of the sesame oil and a few grinds of pepper with the beef. Marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes, never reusing the marinade for anything else. Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.
Meanwhile, stir the gochugaru, lemon juice, the rest of the soy sauce and a spoonful of water together for the sauce.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, drain it and squeeze it dry. Toss it with a little of the sesame oil and the salt.
Pour hot water over the frozen edamame until steaming hot all the way through, then drain, and keep it as its own pile.

Warm a little of the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the carrot, zucchini and mushrooms separately, each for 2 to 4 minutes until just tender, with a pinch of salt, keeping the piles apart.

Cook the beef in the rest of the oil over high heat, in two batches, until browned and at least 71 °C (160 °F), about 3 minutes a batch. Wash your hands, board, knife and tongs after handling the raw beef.
Fry the eggs in the nonstick pan with the last of the olive oil, flip them and cook until the whites and yolks are completely firm, about 4 minutes in all.
Put the rice in bowls and arrange the beef, edamame and vegetables on top in separate piles. Top each with a firm egg, finish with the remaining sesame oil and serve with the sauce to stir through.

Pack the second portion without the egg, with the sauce on the side, into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), then add the sauce. Fry a fresh firm egg to go on top.
recipes.tip: Short on time? Skip the zucchini and use extra spinach. Use less gochugaru for less heat. Put the rice on first.

recipes.name: Yogurt-spiced salmon with kale and chickpea masala over brown basmati
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian tandoori-style fish and chana masala
recipes.about: Salmon fillet marinated in lemony yogurt and warm spices and roasted until flaky, served over brown basmati with a quick tomato, kale and chickpea masala. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the chickpeas and kale bring fibre, iron and calcium.
steps: Mix the yogurt, half of the lemon juice, half of the garam masala, the turmeric, half of the salt and half of the garlic and ginger. Coat the salmon and marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes, never reusing the marinade. Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.

Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a tray. Lift the salmon onto the tray, leaving the extra marinade behind, and roast until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F), 10 to 12 minutes. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds until they sizzle, then the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the rest of the garlic and ginger, the rest of the garam masala and the chili for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, the rest of the salt and a splash of water and simmer until the tomatoes collapse, about 6 minutes. Stir in the kale and simmer until tender, about 5 minutes, then finish with the rest of the lemon juice.
Serve the salmon over the rice with the chickpea masala spooned alongside and the cilantro scattered over.
recipes.tip: Leave out the chili for a mild version. Put the rice on first.

recipes.name: Apple with almonds
recipes.about: A crisp apple with a small handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the almonds.

recipes.name: Turmeric-lemon trout with green herb rice and roast broccoli
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Persian sabzi polo ba mahi, herbed rice with fish
recipes.about: A trout fillet rubbed with turmeric and garlic and roasted next to broccoli, served on brown basmati tossed with kale, parsley, cilantro and dill, with plenty of lemon. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the kale and broccoli bring vitamin C, vitamin K and folate.

ingredients.note: skin on or off, pin bones removed

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the kale, broccoli, parsley and cilantro. Finely chop the kale and the herbs and cut the broccoli into florets.

Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, 25 to 30 minutes, adding the kale for the last 2 minutes. Drain well. Meanwhile, toss the broccoli with a little of the oil and a pinch of the salt on a lined tray and roast for 10 minutes.
Rub the trout with the turmeric, half of the garlic, a little oil, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Push the broccoli to one side, lay the trout on the tray and roast until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F), 10 to 12 minutes.
Warm the rest of the oil and garlic in the empty rice pot for 30 seconds, then tip the rice and kale back in with the dill, parsley, cilantro and half of the lemon juice and stir.
Serve the trout on the herb rice with the broccoli, and squeeze over the rest of the lemon.
recipes.tip: Put the rice on first. No dried dill? Use a little more parsley.

recipes.name: Orange, banana and blueberry cup
recipes.about: Orange segments, sliced banana and blueberries with a squeeze of lemon, a bright snack that packs well. It brings **vitamin C, potassium and fibre**.
steps: Wash the orange and the blueberries. Peel the orange and cut it into segments, and slice the banana.
Toss together with the lemon juice and eat right away, or pack in a lidded tub.
